name: PitchBook
verdict: No OAuth or marketplace review was found. A paid PitchBook subscription with API entitlement is needed and license terms on redistribution and AI use likely apply; mostly unconfirmed, low confidence.
needGuide: Yes — ask PitchBook sales whether a customer-facing AI agent is permitted before building.

auth.detail: No public OAuth app registration or developer portal could be confirmed. Programmatic access is likely a paid add-on to an enterprise subscription (data API or data feeds), provisioned by PitchBook sales or account management with credentials issued to the licensed customer. These details are from background knowledge; none of the pitchbook.com pages tried returned developer content.

effort.timeToFirstTest: unknown (needs a paid subscription and API entitlement first)

approval.gate: The customer (or you, as the licensee) must hold a PitchBook subscription with API entitlement. License terms on redistribution, caching and AI or LLM use likely apply and need review. There is no marketplace or OAuth review to pass.

scopes.why: No scope model confirmed; access follows the licence entitlement.
scopes.summary: No scope model confirmed; access is governed by the licence entitlement (datasets and entities the subscription covers).

cost: Requires a paid PitchBook subscription plus API entitlement (enterprise pricing, amount unknown)
prerequisites: Account and owner: A procurement or business owner who can contract with PitchBook; a developer to store the credentials as secrets.
Where you register: No self-serve console found. The customer's licensed user asks their PitchBook account manager for API access; credentials are issued by PitchBook.
Cost: Requires a paid PitchBook subscription plus API entitlement (enterprise pricing, amount unknown)

registerAt.path: No self-serve console found. The customer's licensed user asks their PitchBook account manager for API access; credentials are issued by PitchBook.

steps.do: Confirm with PitchBook sales whether your intended use (customer-facing AI agent) is permitted by the license
Ask for API access and documentation under the subscription
Receive credentials and store them encrypted, one set per licensed customer
Build a credentials form for customers to paste their own API credentials
Validate with a test query and enforce query and caching limits from the contract
Add monitoring for quota use and credential expiry

roles.team: A procurement or business owner who can contract with PitchBook; a developer to store the credentials as secrets.
roles.customer: The customer's PitchBook admin or licensed user requests API credentials through their account manager; the agent uses credentials the customer supplies.

testing: No sandbox known; ask PitchBook for a trial or test credentials during contracting.

blockers.fix: Every customer needs their own license and entitlement, so plan the sales process.

blockers.problem: License restrictions on redistribution, caching and AI use can block agent features
Cost and quotas are opaque until contracting

automation.agentCan: Draft the licensing questions, build the credential intake and query code once docs and keys are provided, and write tests.
automation.humanMust: Contract and payment with PitchBook, sales conversations, licence review, and issuance of credentials by PitchBook or the customer's admin.

uncertain: Everything: the PitchBook API product name, auth method, entitlement process, pricing, sandbox and AI-use terms.
